messages:
Liam - sales: Quick presales swarm for NexoCorp POC. They've hit repeated stream resets when using our TS SDK behind their corporate proxy. Streaming stops ~14s in with `ECONNRESET`. They saw same with python client.

Nora - solutions: Do we have their SDK versions and a sample request? Also any corporate proxy vendor?

Liam - sales: They use TS SDK v1.4.0 and Python v1.4.0. Proxy is 'corp-edge' appliance (customer can't share vendor yet). Sample request is a normal streaming chat request to /v1/stream with Accept: text/event-stream.

Sam - eng: Logs from customer's TS run?

Liam - sales: Paste from them: 
```
[2026-03-19T09:05:11Z] INFO open stream to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
[2026-03-19T09:05:25Z] ERROR socket hangup after 14.3s
Error: read ECONNRESET
    at TLSWrap.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:XXX)
```

Python client shows: `requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: ("Connection broken: IncompleteRead(0 bytes read)" ,)`.

Diego - infra: On our side we see the connection established and tokens emitted for 90s. No server-initiated close. Sounds like an intermediate device closing idle streams or failing ALPN negotiation on upgrade. Any TLS/intercept or mTLS at their edge?

Liam - sales: Customer says they have TLS inspection enabled and an enterprise TLS terminator in front.

Nora - solutions: Two-pronged repro: 1) Try forcing HTTP/1.1 from client to see if proxy mishandles h2. 2) If TLS inspection is modifying ALPN/ciphers, that can break multiplexed h2 streaming. Ask them to run a raw curl test to compare.

Sam - eng: For TS SDK, we added flag REDWOOD_FORCE_HTTP1 in v1.4.x — they can set it to `1` to force http/1.1 chunked streaming. For Python, set env REDWOOD_HTTP_VERSION=1. Also bump client-side socket/read timeout to 60s. Example for TS: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, streamingKeepaliveMs: 60000 });
process.env.REDWOOD_FORCE_HTTP1 = '1';
```
Note: streamingKeepaliveMs pings connection to keep some proxies from idling out.

Diego - infra: We should also add a server-side header to identify long-lived stream connections (`x-rw-stream: 1`) so support can filter logs faster for these cases. I'll open a ticket.

Nora - solutions: Curl commands to ask customer to run: 
```
# HTTP2 test (expected to fail if proxy is choking h2)
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream

# Force http1.1 test (expected to succeed if proxy can't handle h2)
curl -v --http1.1 --no-keepalive -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Also ask for `openssl s_client -alpn h2 -connect api.redwood.ai:443` output to see ALPN negotiation.

Liam - sales: NexoCorp ran the http1.1 curl and stream stayed open. http2 curl closed at ~14s. `openssl s_client` shows ALPN negotiated to `h2` but with a TLS proxy in between that rewrites handshake.

Sam - eng: That confirms TLS inspection is interfering. Short-term mitigation: force http1.1 or use client keepalive pings. Long-term: recommend Customer use Dedicated/Private route so we terminate TLS directly to their network and avoid MITM appliances.

Diego - infra: I'll add a KB note under presales about TLS-inspection + ALPN causing h2 stream resets and our suggested triage steps. Also create instrumentation to detect repeated `RST_STREAM` patterns.

Nora - solutions: Customer asked about security questionnaire — they want to confirm we don't require non-standard ciphers or custom TLS fingerprinting. Confirm?

Sam - eng: We use standard TLS 1.2/1.3 stacks and default ciphers from the cloud provider. We don't do custom fingerprinting. I'll have Security sign an FAQ line they can include in their questionnaire.

Liam - sales: NexoCorp accepted the http1.1 workaround for the POC. They asked if forcing http1.1 will force us to disable multiplexing for all clients.

Sam - eng: No, forcing http1.1 is per-client. Our hosted endpoints continue to support h2. For POC behind corp proxies it's safe to use http1.1. We'll note the config change in the onboarding doc for presales.

kp-bot: Ticket created: #POC-NEXO-350000  add KB: tls-inspect-alpn-h2, add log header x-rw-stream

Nora - solutions: Next steps: 1) Send step-by-step email with curl tests + env vars for TS/Python. 2) Offer a 10-day Dedicated trial to validate at scale. 3) Provide security FAQ snippet about TLS/ciphers.

Liam - sales: I'll follow up with NexoCorp and close the thread once they confirm POC pass. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
